tasks.title: Gather residency evidence for California REAL ID
Apply for a California REAL ID card

required_documents.text: Bring two different printed California address documents, such as a lease signed by both you and your landlord, utility or mobile phone bill, or a bank record. Check DMV’s address and name instructions, including exceptions.

fees.text: $40 for a regular original ID card. Reduced-fee and no-fee categories have separate eligibility rules.

hours.text: Use the [DMV office finder](https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/locations/) to choose a field office and check its calendar for your visit date.

appointment_rules.text: Visit a DMV office for your first REAL ID. You can start online, make an appointment or check local office wait times.

phone.text: DMV customer service 1-800-777-0133, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. TTY 1-800-368-4327. Choose [Chat with a Live Agent](https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/contacting-dmv/) for online help.

warnings.text: Depending on your situation: if you are using the passport option as proof of identity, bring your unexpired foreign passport, valid U.S. visa and approved I-94, and follow DMV’s original or certified-copy instructions. If your current name differs from your identity document, also bring supporting name-change documents. These depend on your situation and are not part of the document checklist. DMV’s list includes other accepted identity options.
Retrieve your latest electronic I-94 through the official CBP I-94 service and print it if needed.
Official recommendation: use DMV’s full REAL ID checklist before visiting.
DMV also describes a paper application form available at field offices.

If you already have a Social Security number (SSN), provide it to DMV. DMV describes an exemption for legally present applicants who are ineligible for an SSN. Ask DMV how its SSN requirement applies to your REAL ID application. You can ask: “I’m applying for my first California REAL ID card and I don’t have an SSN. Can you tell me whether I can apply in my situation, which documents to bring, and how to book the right appointment?” If your SSN is pending, tell DMV and ask whether you should wait to apply.

For SSA appointment help, call 1-800-772-1213, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. local time in California. TTY 1-800-325-0778. To schedule online, open the [SSA appointment page](https://www.ssa.gov/manage-benefits/make-an-appointment) and select Get started. If you already applied, call and ask: “I applied for an SSN on [date] and I’m still waiting. Can you check whether you need any more documents from me and tell me what I should do next?”
Search by ZIP code in the [SSA office locator](https://www.ssa.gov/locator) for the address, phone number and services of your local office or Card Center.

For your first SSN, start at the [SSA first-time application page](https://www.ssa.gov/number-card/request-number-first-time). Ask SSA: “Hi, I’m an F-1 student applying for a Social Security number for the first time. Can you tell me what documents I need and help me schedule a visit if I need one?”
Want to schedule a first REAL ID visit? Open [DMV appointments](https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/appointments/) and choose First-time REAL ID Application.

tasks.title: Before applying for a driver's license, ask your DSO to confirm your SEVIS record is Active

rules.statement: Retrieve your latest admission record through CBP's official I-94 service and print it if needed.
rules.evidence: See your most recent I-94 form and print it, in case you need your record of legal admission to the U.S.

rules.statement: Check or print your existing I-901 SEVIS fee payment confirmation through the official payment site. Continuing-student and transfer exceptions may apply; this task does not create a new payment obligation.
rules.evidence: print your payment confirmation receipt by going to www.fmjfee.com and selecting Check I-901 Status/Print Payment Confirmation

rules.statement: Contact your school's DSO after entering the United States and follow the school's arrival-reporting instructions. School-specific procedures remain unverified.
rules.evidence: Immediately contact your designated school official (DSO) when you enter the United States.

rules.statement: Report to CRC's International Student Advisor as soon as you arrive. Completing check-in does not confirm SEVIS activation.
rules.evidence: It is important to report to the CRC International Student Advisor as soon as you arrive.

rules.statement: For California REAL ID, prepare two different printed residency documents that meet the official checklist's name, address and exception instructions. This count does not apply to Standard ID; the documents need not come from different institutions.
rules.evidence: To prove that you live in California, you must present TWO DIFFERENT printed documents that show your California mailing address.

rules.statement: Follow California DMV's first-time ID application instructions and complete the required office steps. For REAL ID, follow its identity and residency checklist as well.
rules.evidence: Complete a Driver’s License (DL) or ID Card Application

rules.statement: If you choose to open a U.S. bank account, check the bank's accepted identification, address information, fees and opening requirements. Acceptance of applicants without an SSN varies by provider.
rules.evidence: some banks and credit unions accept foreign passports and consular IDs

rules.statement: Official recommendation — DHS driver's-license guidance: ask your DSO to confirm your SEVIS record is Active before applying for a driver's license. This source does not establish a California REAL ID-card prerequisite. Refer individual immigration-status questions to your DSO.
rules.evidence: Confirming with your DSO that your student record is Active

rules.statement: For CRC Fall 2026 students who enroll on or after July 25, 2026, payment is due the next day after enrollment. These students are not dropped for non-payment, but unpaid fees after the term ends result in a hold on future enrollment until payment is received.
rules.evidence: The next day after enrollment date

rules.statement: California DMV lists a foreign passport with a valid U.S. visa and approved I-94 as one identity option. Follow the original or certified-copy instructions and bring supporting name-change documentation if applicable.
rules.evidence: Unexpired foreign passport with valid U.S. Visa and approved I-94 form

rules.statement: The original regular ID card fee is $40. Separate rates apply to qualifying reduced-fee and no-fee categories.
rules.evidence: ID Card Fees table: Regular ID card / Original / $40

rules.statement: The DMV office finder can locate field offices by ZIP code or city. Use your selected office’s calendar for your visit date.
rules.evidence: Find a location by zip code or city name

rules.statement: First-time REAL ID applicants visit a DMV office. DMV offers online preparation and recommends using the full document checklist before the visit.
rules.evidence: you must visit a DMV office in person when applying for a REAL ID for the first time | We strongly recommend visiting our REAL ID Checklist

rules.statement: DMV provides an online DL/ID application and a paper form at field offices.
rules.evidence: A new paper version of the driver’s license application is available in field offices

rules.statement: California DMV lists customer service and TTY numbers and provides a live chat entry on its contact page.
rules.evidence: Chat with a Live Agent | 1-800-777-0133 | TTY 1-800-368-4327 | Monday – Friday, 8 a.m. – 5 p.m.

rules.statement: DMV describes an SSN exemption for legally present applicants who are ineligible for an SSN. A pending application alone does not establish ineligibility.
rules.evidence: If you are legally present in the U.S., but ineligible for an SSN, you are exempt from the DMV SSN requirement.

rules.statement: CRC publishes an international student email and a number for in-person or phone appointments. The welcome packet accompanies the admission letter and contains arrival information.
rules.evidence: Call (916) 691-7411 if you would like to schedule an in-person or phone appointment.

rules.statement: SSA provides online and phone appointment support. SSA lists 1-800-772-1213 and TTY 1-800-325-0778. Appointment support is available Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. in most U.S. time zones.
rules.evidence: Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. | Call +1 800-772-1213 | Schedule an appointment | Call TTY +1 800-325-0778

rules.statement: The SSA office locator accepts a ZIP code and shows the address, local contact numbers and services of offices or Card Centers.
rules.evidence: Search by address, city, state, or ZIP code | Contact numbers | Card Center

rules.statement: SSA provides an online starting point for a first SSN application in the United States, followed by presentation of documentation at a local office.
rules.evidence: you can apply online, then go to a local Social Security office to provide your documentation

rules.statement: DMV’s appointment service menu lists First-time REAL ID Application.
rules.evidence: First-time REAL ID Application

rules.statement: For CRC Spring 2027, students who enroll on or before December 25, 2026 must pay by January 8, 2027. For enrollment on or after December 26, payment is due the day after enrollment. For the latter group, nonpayment does not cause a drop, but unpaid fees after the term ends place a hold on future enrollment until payment is received.
rules.evidence: December 25, 2026, or earlier | January 8, 2027; December 26, 2026, or later | The next day after enrollment date*
